submission.natural_language_explanation: An induction (successor-copy) head: at a position t it attends to the token that immediately followed the nearest earlier occurrence of the token at t (mean induction weight 0.55 on repeated random sequences, against 0.04 duplicate-token and 0.03 previous-token; in all 20 top examples the peak's attention lands on such a successor, weight 0.44-1.00) and copies that token's value into the residual stream, so its write leaves the resting value exactly where a repeated stretch is being matched and stays there everywhere else. It crosses a quarter of max where a verbatim stretch is being continued - a repeated sentence or clause of roughly eight or more tokens, a repeated code line or block, a repeated markup line, a repeated identifier, string, id or number (scan: syntax 'string' 45% active, 'identifier' 32%, 'comment' 3%), and repeated word pieces inside a repeated multi-piece word (' her' in 'heron', ' snow' in 'snowman') - while first occurrences, non-repeating prose (c4 4.8%, pg19 2.6% active), a lone repeated one-token word ('lantern', 'window', 'turtle'), and case or space variants (' Heron' vs ' heron') stay under the active line.

rival_explanations: A duplicate-token copy head: it fires whenever the current token occurred earlier and copies that earlier occurrence itself, so a lone repeated word in an unrelated context ('the red ball ... the blue ball') activates it as much as a repeated sentence; the near-zero duplicate-token score (0.04) and the fact that every top peak attends to the follower rather than the copy argue against this.

A verbatim-chunk head that needs a multi-token run and is blind to word pieces: it should stay under the line on a single repeated piece and only fire once a whole clause repeats; the top examples' piece peaks ('pected' in 'Expected', 'l' in 'Ullevål', 'up' in 'rupiah', ' her' in 'heron') and repeated multi-piece words that reach half of max argue that pieces are enough.

A token-frequency or token-rarity head: the write tracks how unusual the current token is (token identity explains 25% of the scan's variance), so rare content tokens should fire anywhere; but a lone repeated rare whole word stays at the floor ('lantern', 'window', 'turtle', 'statue' after a repeat all measure 0.02-0.74), and rare tokens in prose with no repeat do not fire.
